title: The Extraction of Kowloon
premise: Hazel Voss, an aviation crash investigator haunted by the loss of their family in the unexplained disaster of Flight 447's row twelve, has spent five years chasing procedural answers in a system that keeps rewriting its own rules. When every digital and paper record of a commercial flight vanishes mid-air — a plane that lands safely but officially never existed — Hazel is pulled into a conspiracy orchestrated by the Meridian Group, a private inheritance empire that engineers 'accidents' to erase inconvenient heirs and rewrite corporate bloodlines. As Hazel uncovers that the vanished flight was a rehearsal for a larger, scheduled attack designed to kill a whistleblower heir and look like pilot error, they must choose between legal justice that will never come and extrajudicial action that could stop it. In the end, Hazel exposes the plot by forcing the attack to happen in a way that leaves living witnesses, sacrifices their career and legal standing to do it, and finally learns the truth about row twelve: their own family was an earlier entry in Meridian's ledger.
about_author: Sebastian Fairweather is the pen name of a former transport-safety journalist who spent a decade covering air disaster inquests across three continents before turning to fiction. They write from a coastal town whose harbor they refuse to name, and they have never once flown without checking the exit rows first.

chapters.title: Row Twelve
chapters.summary: Hazel Voss, POV. Five years after losing their family, Hazel works a routine crash-adjacent docket, reciting procedure like a prayer. A colleague notes Hazel keeps a photograph of row twelve in their case files. Emotional beat: grief disciplined into method; the reader learns Hazel trusts rules because nothing else held.

chapters.title: The Flight That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Flight 882 lands safely, but every record — manifest, telemetry, even the airline's booking logs — has been wiped while it was airborne. Hazel is the first to notice because they were mid-audit on the tail number. Emotional beat: uncanny dread; the machinery Hazel trusted has begun eating its own paper trail.

chapters.title: Rewritten
chapters.summary: Hazel and supervisor Dana Okonkwo, alternating POV. Their inquiry is quietly killed from above; Hazel's access is revoked overnight. Dana warns Hazel to let it go. Emotional beat: institutional betrayal; Hazel realizes the rules were always someone else's rules.

chapters.title: The Passenger List in the Attic
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV, with a flashback thread. Hazel finds a printed boarding pass among their family's belongings — row twelve — and discovers a name on 882's reconstructed manifest that also appeared on their family's flight. Emotional beat: the cold shock of pattern recognition; two disasters, one thread.

chapters.title: Meridian
chapters.summary: New POV: Elias Wren, a fixer for the Meridian Group, cleans up the 882 leak and reports to his unseen principal. We see the cold accounting of human lives as line items. Emotional beat: chilling competence; the antagonist machinery is shown working without malice, which is worse.

chapters.title: The Heir Who Talked
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Hazel tracks the vanished passenger: Ines Calloway, disinherited heir to a Meridian holding company, alive and in hiding. Ines claims 882 was a rehearsal — a dry run for erasing her before she testifies. Emotional beat: wary alliance; two people with nothing left but each other's word.

chapters.title: Procedure Is a Weapon
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Using official channels, Hazel files requests, subpoenas, and safety directives to force records into the open — and watches each one get legally dissolved. Emotional beat: rising fury; the law itself is the conspirator's favorite tool.

chapters.title: Dana's Choice
chapters.summary: Dana Okonkwo, POV. Dana is offered a promotion to bury Hazel's findings and, tormented, copies one file to a burner drive before accepting. Emotional beat: complicity and guilt; the system corrupts good people one signature at a time.

chapters.title: Ledger of Accidents
chapters.summary: Hazel and Ines, POV alternating. Ines reveals Meridian's method: engineered failures timed to inheritance events, decades of them. Hazel cross-references and finds their family's flight in the pattern. Emotional beat: devastation; row twelve was not chance, it was bookkeeping.

chapters.title: The Dry Run's Tail Number
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Forensics on the 882 airframe reveal tampering hardware identical to anomalies in Hazel's family's crash data. Hazel now has physical proof linking past and future. Emotional beat: grim vindication that curdles — proof exists, but no court will touch it.

chapters.title: Wren's Warning
chapters.summary: Elias Wren, POV. Ordered to neutralize Hazel, Wren instead delivers an oblique threat dressed as courtesy — and we glimpse his own doubt. Emotional beat: menace with a hairline crack; the enforcer is not fully owned.

chapters.title: Burned
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Hazel's home is searched, their reputation smeared, Ines's safehouse hit. They barely escape with the tail-number evidence. Emotional beat: terror and loss; the investigation now costs everything, and Hazel pays it anyway.

chapters.title: What Dana Kept
chapters.summary: Dana's POV. Racked with guilt, Dana meets Hazel in secret and hands over the burner drive — a Meridian internal schedule. The next engineered accident has a date: eleven days out. Emotional beat: redemption at a price; Dana knows she has ended her own career.

chapters.title: Eleven Days
chapters.summary: Hazel and Ines, POV. The target flight carries Ines and three other heirs; the plan is a controlled decompression blamed on maintenance fraud. They map the attack's chain: the aircraft, the crew, the certifying inspector. Emotional beat: cold focus; grief has fully hardened into mission.

chapters.title: The Man Who Signs
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Hazel confronts the compromised inspector, a small man drowning in debt, and peels him open. Emotional beat: moral complexity; Hazel uses the same coercive power they despise, and hates how well it works.

chapters.title: Wren's Ledger
chapters.summary: Elias Wren, POV. Wren discovers his own name is on a future Meridian ledger line — he is disposable too. He makes a private copy of the Group's full archive. Emotional beat: self-preservation curdling into defection; corruption devours its own.

chapters.title: The Deal That Isn't
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Hazel brings everything to federal authorities; within hours the case is quashed and a warrant issues for Hazel's arrest. Emotional beat: the death of faith in institutions; justice outside the law is now the only justice on offer.

chapters.title: Boarding
chapters.summary: Hazel, Ines, and Wren, POV rotating. The three conspirators-against-conspiracy board the target flight separately: Hazel as an off-duty inspector, Ines as bait she insisted on being, Wren with the archive and a plan to trigger the evidence dump mid-flight. Emotional beat: dread and resolve at the jet bridge.

chapters.title: Decompression
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV, in-flight. The attack begins — a masked depressurization sequence. Hazel and Wren race the aircraft's own systems, forcing a manual descent and broadcasting the Meridian archive to every newsroom and regulator on the ground before the signal can be cut. Emotional beat: white-knuckle climax; the truth becomes un-erasable at 30,000 feet.

chapters.title: Landing
chapters.summary: Multiple POV. The plane lands with 200 living witnesses and a world already reading the ledger. Meridian's principal is taken into custody abroad; Wren surrenders himself as the archive's source. Emotional beat: exhausted, disbelieving relief — the accident that was supposed to happen became the exposure instead.

chapters.title: The Inquest
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Months later, Hazel testifies at the reopened inquest into their family's flight — as a witness, not an investigator, their career gone, their record expunged but their standing never restored. Emotional beat: bittersweat closure; the truth is public even if Hazel paid everything for it.

chapters.title: Row Twelve, Again
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV, final. Hazel visits the crash memorial, removes the photograph from their files at last, and takes a seat — deliberately — in row twelve of a commercial flight, choosing to fly toward the future rather than be defined by the past. Emotional beat: quiet reclamation; inheritance is what we do with what we're given.
